question_text: Suppose a population is normally distributed with mean $\mu = 30$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 5$. Copy and complete:

subparts.stem: Approximately 68% of the population lies between ...... and 35.

mark_breakdown.desc: Stating the interval within 1 standard deviation of the mean: 25 to 35

subparts.solution: Approximately $68\%$ of the population lies within one standard deviation of the mean, i.e., between $25$ and $35$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The 68-95-99.7 rule states that approximately $68\%$ of data in a normal distribution lies within $\mu \pm \sigma$.

subparts.stem: Approximately 95% of the population lies between 20 and ......

mark_breakdown.desc: Stating the interval within 2 standard deviations of the mean: 20 to 40

subparts.solution: Approximately $95\%$ of the population lies within two standard deviations of the mean, i.e., between $20$ and $40$.

subparts.stem: Approximately ...... of the population lies between 15 and 45.

mark_breakdown.desc: Stating the interval within 3 standard deviations of the mean: 15 to 45

subparts.solution: Approximately $99.7\%$ of the population lies within three standard deviations of the mean, i.e., between $15$ and $45$.

ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Arithmetic errors in multiplying standard deviation.
